title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a 1965 manuscript on the Galois theory of motives. The previous page states a Proposition characterising algebraic numbers λ∈C all of whose conjugates satisfy |λ_α|^2 = Q, for a fixed Q∈Q_{>0}. In modern terms these are Weil Q-numbers of weight 1, the numbers that occur as Frobenius eigenvalues of H^1 of motives over F_q. The equivalent conditions are:
(a) every conjugate has |λ_α|^2 = Q;
(b) λ lies in K or in a totally imaginary quadratic extension (a CM extension) of some totally real number field K, and λλ̄ = Q;
(b') the same with K = Q(a), where a = λ + Q/λ;
(b'') a is totally real, 4Q − a^2 is totally ≥ 0, and λ^2 − aλ + Q = 0;
(c) λ ∈ 𝕃 and λλ̄ = Q. Here 𝕂 is the maximal totally real algebraic extension of Q and 𝕃 is its 'unique' quadratic extension Galois over Q, i.e. the maximal CM field 𝕂(i) = Q^{CM}.

This page finishes the proof.

1. End of b'')⇒b'). Suppose λ ∉ K, i.e. a^2 − 4Q ≠ 0. Then every conjugate satisfies a_α^2 − 4Q ≠ 0, and together with 4Q − a_α^2 ≥ 0 this gives a_α^2 − 4Q < 0. So every root of T^2 − a_αT + Q is non-real and Q(λ) is totally imaginary over the totally real Q(a), i.e. a CM extension.

2. b')⇒b) is trivial.

3. b)⇒c). 𝕂(λ) is 𝕂 or a totally imaginary quadratic extension of 𝕂, hence lies in 𝕂(i).

4. c)⇒a). Since 𝕃 is Galois over Q, every conjugate λ_α = σ_α(λ) lies in 𝕃. Complex conjugation generates Gal(𝕃/𝕂), so λ̄_α is the unique 𝕂-conjugate of λ_α. Hence λ_α λ̄_α = N_{𝕃/𝕂}(λ_α) = σ_α(N_{𝕃/𝕂}(λ)) = σ_α(Q) = Q.

5. Crossed-out Corollary (abandoned). Every subfield L ⊂ 𝕃 would be generated by some λ with λλ̄ = Q, integral if Q∈Z.

6. It is replaced by a Remark. Let K be a totally real number field and Q∈Q with Q > 1. Then there exist a CM extension L/K and an integer i ≥ 1 such that L is generated by an element λ with λλ̄ = Q^i, i.e. by a Weil Q^i-number; λ can be taken integral if Q∈Z.
   - Proof: choose a primitive element a of K, which can be taken integral. Choose i so large that 4Q^i − a^2 is totally positive; this is possible because Q > 1 and K has finitely many real embeddings.
   - Let λ be a root of λ^2 − aλ + Q^i = 0. Then Q(λ) contains a = λ + Q^i/λ, hence contains K, and λ is totally non-real. So L = Q(λ) is a CM extension of K, and λ is integral when a and Q are.

Purpose: the page determines the fields generated by Weil numbers (they are exactly CM or totally real fields). It also shows that over every totally real field there are CM extensions generated by Weil numbers. This is the arithmetic input for describing the 'motivic Galois group' of motives over finite fields via Weil numbers, i.e. the Weil-number torus later formalised by Serre, Langlands–Rapoport and Milne.
errors: (c) speaks of 'the unique quadratic extension of 𝕂 Galois over Q'. The correct and intended characterisation is 'the unique totally imaginary quadratic extension of 𝕂', namely 𝕂(√−1). If d∈𝕂 is totally positive then √d∈𝕂, so every CM-type quadratic extension equals 𝕂(i). Uniqueness among all Galois quadratic extensions is not justified.
The Remark's integrality claim needs a to be an algebraic integer. Grothendieck adds this afterthought ('on peut supposer a entier'), and it is harmless.

Thread continues on the next page with a genuine error. There it is claimed that λ' = λ^{1/i} also lies in L, giving a Weil Q-number (not Q^i-number) generating a CM field containing K. An i-th root of λ need not lie in L, and Q(λ^{1/i}) need not be CM. The standard remedy (Honda–Tate) is to pass to F_{q^i} rather than extract roots.

Minor gap: the Remark only produces some CM extension of K, not a prescribed one. The crossed-out Corollary (every subfield of 𝕃 generated by a Weil Q-number) was abandoned, presumably for this reason.

ideas.what: An algebraic number with all conjugates of absolute value √Q (Weil number) lies in a CM field or a totally real field; equivalently λ∈Q^{CM} with λλ̄ = Q.
ideas.modern_name: Weil q-numbers lie in CM fields (maximal CM field Q^{CM} = Q^{tr}(i))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore around Weil and Honda–Tate (Tate 1966/68, Honda 1968); standard in Milne's and Serre's accounts of motives over finite fields

ideas.what: Proof of c)⇒a) using the norm N_{𝕃/𝕂} and the centrality of complex conjugation in Gal(Q^{CM}/Q).
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation is central in the Galois group of a CM field

ideas.what: Any totally real K admits a CM extension L generated by a Weil Q^i-number: take λ a root of T^2 − aT + Q^i with 4Q^i − a^2 totally positive.
ideas.modern_name: Existence of Weil numbers generating CM fields (cf. Honda–Tate realisation of CM fields)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard construction; related to Honda–Tate theory (1966–68)

missed.claim: Documents that already in 1965 Grothendieck, while building the Galois theory of motives, worked out the CM-field characterisation of Weil numbers. This is the arithmetic seed of the later 'Weil number torus' description of the motivic Galois group over F_q. It is historically interesting for dating, but mathematically routine.
missed.quote: c) ⇒ a) car si λ_α = σ_α(λ), on aura λ_α ∈ 𝕃, donc λ̄_α est l'unique conjugué de λ_α sur 𝕂
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It helps date Grothendieck's awareness of Q^{CM} as the field of definition of Weil numbers, before Honda–Tate and Serre's motivic Galois-group descriptions.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, elementary characterisation of Weil numbers via CM fields, plus a simple existence construction. Both are standard and essentially folklore; the only interest is historical (1965 dating). The continuation on the next page contains an error.
transcription_corrections: In (c) and here, 𝕃 should be understood as the maximal CM field 𝕂(i); the transcription is fine, but 'unique' refers in substance to the totally imaginary quadratic extension.
'(il est possible [?] car Q∈Q, Q>1)' likely reads '(i existe car Q∈Q, Q>1)' or similar — the point is the existence of such i.
'{+on peut supposer a entier.+}' is a marginal insertion attached to the sentence 'Si Q∈Z, on peut prendre λ entier algébrique'.
The final words are uncertain; the sense is 'si Q est entier (et a entier), il est entier'.
